data.title: How to start a run club in Mumbai
data.lead: A route, a time, a café at the end and a plan for the people who come alone. Everything you need for your first five runs.

sections.h: Pick a route people can find
paras: Start and finish at the same place, ideally a café that opens early. Sea-face promenades work because they’re flat, lit and easy to describe.
list: Under 5 km for the first few runs
One meeting point, the same every week
A loop, so nobody gets lost
sections.tip: Walk the route at the same time of day before your first run. Note where people can regroup.

sections.h: Choose a time and stick to it
paras: Early weekend mornings beat the heat and the traffic. The same time every week matters more than the perfect time.

sections.h: Plan for the person who comes alone
paras: Most newcomers come on their own. If they end up at the back by themselves, they don’t come back.
list: Put people in pace groups of six to eight
Give each group a lead who says hello
Ask one easy question before you set off
sections.tip: On Catch, runners book with a pace and groups are planned for you, with newcomers spread out.

paras: Run one: friends and friends of friends. Runs two and three: post the route and the café. Runs four and five: ask regulars to bring one person each, with their own link so you know who brought whom.
Keep social runs free. Charge for coached sessions, races and anything with coffee or a coach included. Paid runs have fewer no-shows; free runs grow faster.
sections.tip: Free runs stay free on Catch. Paid runs are 5% of ticket sales, never more than ₹10,000 a month.

aside.title: Start your club on Catch
aside.body: Sign-ups, pace groups, a first hello and next week’s run, without the WhatsApp thread.
